supporting_observations.claim: The alerted failures repeatedly target svc-render from FILE-NWD-01, with the workstation name also FILE-NWD-01 and the reported process C:\Windows\System32\lsass.exe; this pattern is consistent across the records.

The failures continue at roughly one-minute intervals after the scheduled 13:30 UTC password rotation, matching the inventory description that RenderQueue re-authenticates each run and must be updated manually after rotation.
The authentication records report bad-password status 0xc000006a; the supplied evidence shows repeated failures, not a successful authentication.

The same periodic svc-render failures were already occurring before the scheduled rotation, beginning at 13:31 UTC, which is consistent with a job continuing to use an outdated credential rather than evidence of a new external logon source.

known_telemetry_limitations: The provided records end at 13:46 UTC, so they do not cover the remainder of the requested 13:20–14:20 UTC window.
The authentication events identify LSASS as the process but do not establish which service or job supplied the credentials.
The records show failed attempts but do not establish whether the password rotation occurred or whether the RenderQueue job was subsequently updated.
claims_not_established: Whether the scheduled password rotation was completed at 13:30 UTC.
Whether the RenderQueue configuration still held the old password at the time of the failures.
Whether svc-render authenticated successfully later in the requested window.
Whether any unlogged activity occurred on FILE-NWD-01.
additional_evidence_needed: For operational confirmation, verify the password-rotation completion and RenderQueue credential update against the change record and job configuration.
